history.rationale: Surface cationic residue in the m102.4 epitope region; alanine removes a likely antibody contact while not being a major ephrin-binding anchor.

High phenotype (0.81) and good structure compatibility (0.73) support antibody escape potential and structural acceptance, despite low sequence plausibility. Retain as a top candidate though slightly below Y511F/W503F.
Highest phenotype among all candidates and good structure compatibility, despite moderate sequence plausibility.
Adjacent to a reported antibody footprint; loss of the lysine side chain may impair m102.4 recognition while preserving receptor binding.
Similar to K499A, high escape and moderate structure, with slightly better sequence plausibility. Ranked slightly below K499A due to lower structure compatibility.
High phenotype but slightly lower structure compatibility; still a viable candidate.
Aromatic residue at the antibody-receptor interface; replacing tryptophan with phenylalanine retains aromatic packing but changes the epitope surface for m102.4.
Excellent sequence plausibility and structure compatibility, but phenotype is moderate (0.62). Strong viability and likely good folding; keep high despite lower escape than K499A/K501A.
Excellent structure compatibility and top sequence plausibility with acceptable phenotype.
Tyrosine-to-phenylalanine removes a polar/aromatic antibody contact while preserving steric volume and likely hydrophobic receptor interactions.

Best combined profile: top structure compatibility (0.82), high sequence plausibility (0.91), moderate-high escape (0.70). Also appears in natural homologs (MSA z=0.2), indicating conservation tolerance. Top candidate.
Best overall balance: highest structure compatibility and very high sequence plausibility, with strong antibody escape phenotype.
Predicted surface residue near the m102.4 contact zone; alanine reduction may disrupt antibody recognition with modest effect on ephrin binding.
Moderate structure (0.69) and some evolutionary tolerance (MSA z=0.286), but lower escape (0.53). Retain with moderate confidence; may be lower priority.
Low phenotype and modest structural support; unlikely to meet escape goal.
Aromatic side chain likely contacts the antibody paratope; removal may lower m102.4 affinity but could still retain protein stability.
Low phenotype (0.45) and very low structure compatibility (0.24). Poor candidate for both escape and viability.

history.rationale: Exposed residue within the m102.4 footprint; small alanine substitution may perturb antibody contacts without perturbing the receptor site.

Excellent structural compatibility but weak phenotype; not prioritized.
Neighbor of K499/K501 in the putative m102.4 epitope; alanine substitution may reduce mAb contacts while maintaining ephrin recognition.
